pairs.subject: remediation-roadmaps
pairs.evidence: src/lib/scoring/projections.ts:162 The next-level planner selects whole-dimension closures by weighted headroom without considering effort or reporting total cost, so its advertised cheapest path does not minimize effort.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/scoring/projections.ts:162 The planner correctly re-scores combinations and checks ceiling reachability, but selects dimensions without recommendation effort estimates and returns no total effort.

src/components/report/RecommendationTracker.tsx:88 The generation pass appends follow-ups for uncovered weak dimensions, but gives them no coverage provenance; this tracker re-sorts every item together and renders coverage items with ordinary priority numbering and quick-win badges.

src/lib/scoring/recommendations.ts:403 The shared generation funnel deterministically records imperative, supervisory, and contradictory wording without rejecting or rewriting findings; catalog titles are observational, and tracking supports dismissal with an optional reason and carries dismissed status across scans.

src/components/report/RoadmapSandbox.tsx:237 Trying any recommendation assigns its entire dimension a perfect score, without a move-specific achievable target or confidence discount; shared scoring avoids additive totals but does not make this impact assumption conservative.

src/components/report/RoadmapSandboxCommit.tsx:151 Commit is explicit, but its result retains only aggregate counts; failed recommendation identities and rejection reasons are not retained or displayed per item, contrary to the required partial-failure state model.

src/components/report/roadmapPriority.tsx:18 The tracker's default ordering uses categorical impact and effort rather than rubric weight × achievable headroom × achievability; it overrides the fallback generator's weighted ordering and has no stable-identity tie-break.
